{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZjXWBw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhDKFYM", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 85, "title": "Implement single-head multi-sector µPD765 non-DMA WRITE DATA", "body": "## Problem

Non-DMA WRITE DATA currently accepts only R=EOT. Commands requesting multiple sectors on one head return invalid-command status instead of requesting payload, preventing raw floppy clients from performing ordinary sequential writes.

At baseline `829e070d66d06d25c46b4c32ea5710d0c3b0a069`, [Bus::finish_fdc](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/829e070d66d06d25c46b4c32ea5710d0c3b0a069/src/bus.rs#L967) explicitly rejects write commands with R≠EOT. The shared PIO scheduler already resolves successive sector IDs, and the write path counts each sector receiving payload. This makes multi-sector writes a bounded extension of the completed single-sector implementation.

## Expected outcome

VM and Ap execute MFM WRITE DATA (`45h`) with SPECIFY ND=1, MT=0, matching selected head/H, N=1–3 and 1≤R≤EOT, using the existing two drives and normal raw/D88 media. A command writes successive sectors on the selected cylinder/head through EOT without requiring another command between sectors.

### Hardware contract

- Match C/H/R/N, transfer `128 << N` bytes per sector, and increment R between sectors while retaining C/H/N. DTL does not shorten transfers when N is nonzero. NEC describes this as multi-sector writing and applies READ DATA’s termination rules to WRITE DATA. See the [NEC µPD765 functional descriptions, WRITE DATA and READ DATA](https://datasheet4u.com/pdf/1098399/UPD765.pdf).
- Preserve MSR waiting/ready states `30h/B0h`, one byte per ready write, and result/idle states `D0h/80h`. Use seven results in ST0/ST1/ST2/C/H/R/N order. Missing requested sectors set ST1.ND=`04h`; protected media sets NW=`02h`; missed interior-byte service sets OR=`10h`. See [NEC µPD765A/B Tables 2–4](https://hxc2001.com/download/datasheet/floppy/thirdparty/FDC/NEC/UPD765_Datasheet_OCRed.pdf#page=9).
- Each execution-byte request interrupts; its servicing write acknowledges the FDC request. Completion generates a separate result interrupt, acknowledged by the first result read. Drain all results before accepting another command. See the [NEC processor-interface description](https://datasheet4u.com/pdf/1098399/UPD765.pdf).
- Preserve the repository’s deterministic timing: 160 clocks for dispatch, first request 128 clocks later, subsequent requests every 128 clocks including sector boundaries, and timeout after 104 unserviced clocks. These are emulator scheduling choices derived from NEC’s normal 16 µs and worst-case 13 µs MFM intervals, not a mechanical-timing claim. See [NEC Application Note 8, PDF page 2](https://hxc2001.com/download/datasheet/floppy/thirdparty/FDC/NEC/uPD765_App_Note_Mar79.pdf#page=2).

Retain the existing documented EOT-without-TC result policy: `[40h | drive | (H<<2), 80h, 00h, C, H, EOT, N]`. The final-ID choice is the repository’s interpretation of NEC’s EOT/EN and result-field descriptions, not independently measured hardware evidence. The functional description’s processor-termination table addresses a different termination path. Preserve the existing logical-image policy for interrupted writes: accepted payload remains; unaccepted bytes and metadata remain unchanged. See [the current FDC contract](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/829e070d66d06d25c46b4c32ea5710d0c3b0a069/docs/hardware.md#fdc-non-dma-write-data).

### Focused scope and remaining work

Implement single-head sector progression using the current PIO machinery. This Issue does not add MT/head switching, N=0/DTL transfers, deleted-data/format/scan/diagnostic commands, TC/EOP injection, full SPECIFY timing, new media formats, 512-byte IPL support, active BIOS preemption, comprehensive board controls, or CRC/flux/mechanical fidelity. The µPD765A/B final-byte overrun distinction remains unverified; new timeout acceptance should target first/interior requests. These remain explicit FDC work after this Issue.

## Context and reproduction

Source inspection predicts this reproduction on either profile with writable 77×2×8×1024 raw media:

1. Enable the existing FDC board path with port `94h = 18h`.
2. Send SPECIFY `[03h, DFh, 03h]` through port `92h`; allow dispatch to finish.
3. Send WRITE DATA `[45h, 00h, 00h, 00h, 02h, 03h, 03h, 1Bh, FFh]`.
4. Advance through dispatch and the first-byte boundary; inspect port `90h`.

Current source produces result-phase `D0h` and one-byte invalid-command `80h`. Expected behavior is `B0h`, followed by requests for 2,048 payload bytes and one final seven-byte result. This evaluator did not execute the reproduction.

[Existing tests](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/829e070d66d06d25c46b4c32ea5710d0c3b0a069/tests/fdc.rs#L866) explicitly reject the R=2/EOT=3 case. Replace that obsolete expectation while preserving invalid-range and unrelated command rejection coverage.

Issue #83/PR #84 completed single-sector writes; this proposal extends their deliberately excluded multi-sector behavior. The supplied open-Issue list is empty. The Coordinator reports 335 native tests and 118 production-Wasm browser cases passing after the media-replacement fix; independent PR review and remote CI were not supplied. See [the recorded validation](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/829e070d66d06d25c46b4c32ea5710d0c3b0a069/docs/validation.md#issue-83-review-fix-media-replacement-during-pio-execution).

All 26 inventory categories retain their supplied scopes and statuses: 23 partial, GRCG implemented_unverified, paging/FPU unimplemented, none verified. Protected mode, paging and basic x87 remain required. Missing evaluator-checkout fixtures do not block this plan; limited probes and six-game reports establish neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

The Coordinator performs implementation and validation before merge.

- [ ] Add a regression reproducing the R=2/EOT=3 rejection on the baseline, then demonstrate execution through the specified contract. Replace only the obsolete multi-sector rejection expectation; retain R=0, R>EOT and unrelated unsupported-variant checks.
- [ ] Add clocked port-level tests on VM and Ap covering both drives/heads, D88 N=1–3 and all three existing raw geometries. Exercise two-sector and longer ranges, a nonzero cylinder after seek, and EOT at the physical track end. Use distinct sector payloads and independently calculated image offsets. Compare complete selected/other-drive images, including all D88 headers and untouched sectors. Count each sector receiving payload exactly once.
- [ ] Verify sector boundaries remain in execution: no intermediate result or extra command, no repeated/skipped payload, correct byte direction and request acknowledgment, and one final result interrupt. Exercise real cascaded PIC delivery and both EOIs; held requests must not retrigger after EOI. Early/duplicate writes and wrong-direction reads must preserve the pending request.
- [ ] Test timing immediately before/at the next-sector request boundary, service at 103 clocks, timeout at 104 clocks, and equivalent split/batched ticks including overshoot. Port polling must not advance guest time or move request deadlines.
- [ ] Test a missing later ID using original valid D88 media, a later N mismatch, and EOT beyond available raw sectors. Preserve completed writes, stop at the unavailable ID, return the specified ND result with the failing requested CHRN, and leave later sectors untouched. Confirm protected-media rejection and fresh-command recovery.
- [ ] Interrupt execution after one completed sector and before/after accepting a prefix in the next sector. Cover timeout, reset, eject and selected-drive replacement, including waiting/ready requests. Compare complete removed/replacement images; retain only accepted bytes and correct write counts. Replacement must cancel stale execution before another byte reaches new media, while changing the other drive must preserve the active transfer.
- [ ] Extend DMA-isolation coverage to multi-sector execution with enabled/unmasked and disabled/masked DMA. Preserve current/base addresses/counts, bank, mode, masks, controller enable, shared byte pointer, sticky TC and guarded RAM. After completion, verify idle-controller BIOS DMA readback and subsequent ND=1 PIO reentry. Retain existing ND=0 DMA and BIOS-handoff regressions.
- [ ] Add an original MIT source-built guest probe with an offline builder and pinned provenance manifest, for example `guest/fdc_write_multi.asm`, `tools/prepare_fdc_write_multi_fixture.py` and `fixtures/fdc-write-multi-manifest.json`. The guest must issue one R=2/EOT=3 write, then read back both sectors through PIO, servicing actual byte/result interrupts and EOIs itself. Require exactly 2,048 byte requests per direction, one result interrupt per command, exact result records, distinct payloads, guards and restored stack. Hosts may mount, step, inspect and reset; expected results/media must come from independent fixture oracles. Pin source/license, assembly, firmware/image hashes and a 2,000,000-slot budget. Use no commercial software or proprietary ROMs.
- [ ] Run that identical probe natively and in production release-Wasm on VM and Ap, before/after reset, with browser coverage at `/` and `/pc98-rust/`. Compare complete exported media and guarded guest records. Preserve the existing single-sector probe, DOS/apps/VM/audio, IDE-edge and six-game assertions and budgets. Wire the new fixture into the existing preparation/CI flow.
- [ ] Following README preparation guidance with original/licensed assets, pass `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p test_fixture_fetch.py`, the new offline fixture builder, `cargo test --locked --test fdc --test fdc_bios --test core --test dma --test pic`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and `npm test`. If occupied ports require a temporary configuration, preserve both serving paths, scenarios, assertions and budgets and report the exact command. Update hardware documentation and validation evidence with actual outcomes and remaining limitations; do not mark the whole FDC category verified.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
